articleTitle: What the clients really think (quality control consultancy)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Management Consultancy and ISO 9000
abstract: This paper is based a regional study of quality practices in Northern Ireland, conducted between March and September 1992. The findings are based on responses from a representative sample of 2037 organisations in both the public and private sectors, employing 10 or more people. The overall objective of the survey was to establish the current levels of activity with respect to both ISO 9000 and total quality management in the province. It is in this context that part of the study examines the involvement of quality consultants.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Selecting the right consultant (for quality control)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Management Consultancy and ISO 9000
abstract: The author examines the problem of selecting the right consultant to assist a company with obtaining registration to ISO 9000. In order to address this particular issue, the author first clarifies a few points regarding the relationship between a quality management system, ISO 9000 and a business management system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: And ISO 9000 applies to consultants as well! (quality control)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Management Consultancy and ISO 9000
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to outline some of the practical issues associated with applying ISO 9000 to a consultancy organisation; and to highlight some of the practical benefits impacting on consultants and clients alike.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Making effective use of consultancy support (for quality control)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Management Consultancy and ISO 9000
abstract: There are any number of reasons to use consultancy resources during an ISO 9000 implementation including: to help with project management; to provide technical expertise in the interpretation of the standard into business practice; to develop and deliver training programmes; and finally, to provide practical experience. Most companies only carry out one ISO 9000 implementation, therefore avoiding mistakes and cutting down the learning curve by using practical experience can be a good investment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
